clue.text: My job, as pal badly spelled out, is to make night attire

indicators.note: the words are spelt out afresh, so their letters are set down in a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of the phrase are used

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that their task is to produce nightwear because a friend wrote out the order poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'spelled out' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby-doll pyjamas are a short, loose style of women's nightwear, so they are a kind of night attire.

clue.text: Bird with a grub flying around cloudy ridge

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed around the other, enclosing it
letters flying about are scattered and land in a new order
something cloudy is murky and mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird with a caterpillar in its beak flies about a misty hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate anagrams here, one wrapped inside the other, each with its own signal word.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, a popular pet bird.

clue.text: Women need beauty treatment as a private matter

indicators.note: a treatment works something over, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: all fifteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A confidential remark that women require salon pampering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when sharing a confidence, meaning the remark should stay private.

clue.text: Girl heard too, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: all eight letters are used

explanation.surface: A girl regrets that she was overheard as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts a homophone, but the words are simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothea is a female first name, and 'girl' in crosswords often stands for any girl's name.

clue.text: City in Belgium for example featured in story

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a story is an untruth, a lie
the usual abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A Belgian city is given as an example in a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a major city in eastern Belgium, in the French-speaking Wallonia region.

clue.text: A medley of popular tunes could be up to prior

indicators.note: these words say what the letters could become if arranged differently

parts.note: all nine letters are used

explanation.surface: A monastery's prior might get up to some singing of a medley of hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-pourri is a mixed collection, used especially of a musical piece stringing together various tunes.

clue.text: Jack has quarrel in port

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack gets into an argument in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' reads as an argument, but here it is the old word for a crossbow bolt. JARROW is a port town on the Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Jarrow is a town on the River Tyne with docks, historically known for shipbuilding.

clue.text: Talking idly about one extremely youthful crime

indicators.note: one word goes about the others, surrounding them

parts.note: maundering means rambling or talking aimlessly
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Idle chatter about a young person's misdeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laundering is the offence of passing illegally obtained funds through legitimate channels to hide their source.

clue.text: Fix a casserole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a difficult or anxious state
second meaning: a dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as a verb, as if mending or preparing the dish; it is the noun meaning a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew means being in a fix or flustered state, and a stew is also a slow-cooked dish.

clue.text: Cleansing agent put off squire

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
a squire is a gentleman, informally a gent

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that a country gentleman finds off-putting.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a substance used for washing, a chemical that removes dirt.

clue.text: Phoned leader of expedition for compass

parts.note: rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone rang the expedition's head to ask for a compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the navigational instrument, but here it means scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent of reach is a synonym of range.

clue.text: Happening just before start of tournament

parts.note: even can mean just, as in 'even as I spoke'

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something occurs shortly before a tournament gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just before' tempts EVE, the day before; but 'just' alone is the piece and 'before' only places it ahead of the next letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or something that takes place, a noun synonym of happening.

clue.text: Saving made by company that's invested in foreign money

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other
something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take on an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm puts its funds into overseas currency to cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign money' reads as currency, but 'foreign' rearranges the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means thrift or careful avoidance of waste, the same as a saving.

clue.text: Fails to hear husband in pothole, bringing narrow escape

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed in the last, so it surrounds them

parts.note: a pothole is a deep cave, as explored by potholers
to lose someone's words is to fail to catch them
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A caver whose spouse can't hear him down in a hole has a lucky escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pothole' suggests a road defect, but in Britain it is also a deep cave, hence the sport of potholing.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a narrow escape from danger, like a razor just missing the skin.

clue.text: Publicans in the North needing minders

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north
minders are people who look after something, keepers

explanation.surface: Landlords of northern pubs need bouncers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the North' reads as a location, but 'in' is a piece in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, an establishment once called an inn, so innkeepers is a synonym.

clue.text: Tested about Latin language

parts.note: something proven has been tried and tested
CA is short for circa, Latin for about
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: Someone examined in Latin is checked on a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal, but it supplies CA, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal is the Romance language of Provence in southern France, a form of Occitan.

clue.text: Book to attend every single social function

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
every single one means all of them

explanation.surface: Reserving tickets so that every unattached person can go to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To attend' places the second piece beside the first rather than meaning go to; 'Book' is a noun, not the verb reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal dance, a classic example of a grand social occasion.

clue.text: Want, in new base, a source of water

indicators.note: the first word is placed in the reworked letters that follow
something new is made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
want means a shortage, a lack

explanation.surface: A new military base is short of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is a large inland sea between Europe and Asia, a body of water.

clue.text: A cat, tiny thing

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone describes a kitten as a tiny thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, so the word is used for anything minute.

clue.text: Caron (& Louis) cast in play

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould, so the letters are thrown into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two actors, Leslie Caron and a Louis, are chosen for parts in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as theatrical casting, which fits the play, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus is one of Shakespeare's Roman tragedies, a stage play.

clue.text: Article supporting bogus doctor-priest

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece holds the other up from below, so the article is written second

parts.note: something bogus is a sham
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs a fraudulent medic who claims holy powers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece supporting another sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer believed to work through the spirit world, both medicine man and priest.

clue.text: A permit held by the sportsman

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A sportsman holds a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like part of the definition, but it is a piece of the wordplay that wraps round the permit.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, a sportsman.

clue.text: Dread (after opener's dismissal) making a mistake

indicators.note: dismissing the opener, as in cricket, sends off the first letter

parts.note: dread is great fear, terror

explanation.surface: A batsman's fear of getting out, after the opener goes, leads to a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is the first batsman; here it is the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is an error, a straightforward synonym for something done wrongly.

clue.text: Caught, she's out in game

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cricketer reports that she was caught and dismissed during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' and 'out' read together as a cricket dismissal, but they do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game of strategy for two players.

clue.text: Learn about head of muscovy duck

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, wrapping around it

parts.note: to see is to learn or find out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Find out about the top of a Muscovy duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscovy duck' reads as one bird, but 'duck' alone is the definition; a smee is a dialect name for a duck such as the smew or wigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is an old regional name for certain ducks, such as the smew or pintail.

clue.text: Electronic device in fashion — millions after it

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A trendy gadget sells by the million.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device that converts signals so that computers can communicate over a telephone line.

clue.text: A Swedish queen creating terrible stir in country

indicators.note: the reworked letters are placed in the country's name

parts.note: a country

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so these letters are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian monarch causes an awful commotion abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina reigned as Queen of Sweden in the 17th century before abdicating and moving to Rome.

clue.text: Upset learning a letter reveals an emotional relationship

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters are used

explanation.surface: Distressed at finding a letter that exposes an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The eternal triangle is the stock love triangle of two people competing for a third, a fraught romantic situation.
